title: Three A2/A3 multiply-add precision paths into an initialized accumulator
surface: muladddst(dst, a, b) accumulating into its destination, with adds(dst, c, 0.0) initializing it; the mixed path's repeat=, dst_blk_stride=, src1_blk_stride=, src2_blk_stride=, dst_rep_stride=, src1_rep_stride=, src2_rep_stride= form; four separate DBuff two-slot UB allocations; one kernel source across the a2 and a3 facades
study_for: `muladddst` accumulates into its destination. The destination is the accumulator, not a third operand, so `adds(acc, c, 0.0)` has to put `c` there first -- and `check_domain` refuses an input whose `c` is all zero, because then a kernel that skipped that step would agree anyway. Reading this as a three-operand FMA is the mistake the interface invites.

Four separate two-slot buffers, and the separation is the point. a, b and c are filled by MTE2; only the vector pipeline writes the accumulator. Mixing those roles onto one buffer is the defect this arrangement was reviewed to fix, and the 40,000-element case -- 157 tiles over two slots -- is what stops it from passing by luck.

The mixed path is in repeat mode, and the strides are per-dtype. `repeat = ceil(valid / 64)`, the FP32 destination steps 8 blocks per repeat and the FP16 sources step 4. Those numbers come from the element widths, not from the shapes, so they do not survive a dtype change. (Prose in the archive describing a count mode for this body is stale; the corrected body is the repeat form.)

The final repeat computes past the valid lanes on purpose, inside the fixed 5,120-element allocation, and only the logical prefix is published. `n65_tile64` has a second tile with one valid lane and 63 scratch lanes; `n5121_tile5120` is the largest allocation with the smallest second tile, which is where an overrun would land outside the buffer. A shared model calculation once checked a 5,184-element footprint for the valid 5,120-element tile; M10-036 repaired that.

The three bounds are per path and the reference is FP64. 1e-4 for the all-FP32 path and 2e-3 where the sources are FP16, each with a matching relative L2 bound so that a uniform bias cannot hide inside the element allowance. The dyadic cases make the arithmetic exact, so five of the ten cases do not depend on the budget at all.
do_not_copy_when: You want `dst = a * b`. Then the initialization is wrong and you need a plain multiply. `muladddst` always adds to what is there.

Your dtypes differ from these three pairs. The mixed path's repeat strides are derived from a 4-byte destination and 2-byte sources; another combination needs its own numbers, and getting them wrong computes the right values into the wrong lanes.
You are reading the 2e-3 bound as FP16 accuracy. It is the bound these inputs need in this operation order, over values in [-2, 2]. It is not a general statement about half precision.

Your allocation is sized to the valid length. The final repeat writes scratch lanes up to the next multiple of 64, so the buffer has to have them. Here they are always inside the 5,120-element allocation, and two cases exist to keep that true.
